text:
Predicates:
SupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
UnsupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
UsedToTrain(x, y) ::: x is used to train y.
StateOfTheArtModel(y) ::: y is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
Train(y, x) ::: y is trained with x.
PublishedIn(y, year) ::: y was published in year.
Premises:
∀x (UnsupervisedLearning(x) → ¬UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtModel)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data for training the model.
UsedToTrain(stateOfTheArtModel, x) → ¬ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art model.
Train(stateOfTheArtModel, y) → RequiresLabelledData(y) ::: The training of the model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
UnsupervisedLearning(x) ∧ UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtModel) ::: Unsupervised learning is used to train the model.
